answer: Lock a time-delayed bond for each agent identity before it can earn, so to forge a new identity costs real stake, compute, and waiting time rather than a free copy. Like a tide, the bond cost rises with each additional identity from the same operator, so a thousand fakes must pay a thousand times and cannot share one deposit. Random peer checks act as a zephyr that exposes lockstep voting or copied work, slashing the bond and erasing the fake identities earnings before they can cash out.
